'''Dame Julia Stretton Higgins''' (née '''Downes'''; born 1 July 1942) is a British [[polymer scientist]].  Since 1976, she has been based at the Department of [[Chemical Engineering]] at [[Imperial College London]], where (since 2007) she is {{lang|la|[[:wikt:emeritus|emeritus]]}} professor and senior research investigator.<ref name="whoswho"/><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=7402119724}}</ref><ref name="personal webpage">{{cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/AP/faces/pages/read/Home.jsp?person=j.higgins&_adf.ctrl-state=12wlum3ndv_131&_afrRedirect=1728436067837551|title=Dame Julia Higgins profile|access-date=18 April 2014}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ingenia.org.uk/ingenia/articles.aspx?Index=423 Professor Dame Julia Higgins' profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924035139/http://www.ingenia.org.uk/ingenia/articles.aspx?Index=423 |date=24 September 2015 }}, ''Ingenia'', September 2007</ref><ref>{{YouTube|id=MBFIXB2kTjw|title=Symposium Opening speech by Julia Higgins 2008}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|id=XwSe1nQaiQ4|title=The Royal Society's The Vision Committee's Vision for the future of Science and Maths Education}}, chaired by Julia Higgins</ref>

==Education==
Higgins was educated at the [[Ursuline High School, Wimbledon]] and [[Somerville College, Oxford]] where she was awarded [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|Master of Arts]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] degrees.<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Julia Stretton|last=Higgins |title=Inelastic scattering of neutrons from clathrate inclusion compounds and molecules in molecular sieves |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1968 |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph020545024 |website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk }}</ref><ref name="British Library">{{cite web
|title=Life Stories in association with the British Library
|url=http://sounds.bl.uk/related-content/TRANSCRIPTS/021T-C1379X0055XX-0000A1.pdf
|access-date= 1 December 2016
|website=Sounds.bl.uk
}}</ref><ref name=tls>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b083n2jg|title=Julia Higgins on polymers, interview on The Life Scientific|first=Jim|last=Al-Khalili|author-link=Jim Al-Khalili|year=2016|publisher=BBC|website=bbc.co.uk|location=London}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1999, Higgins was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for the application of neutron scattering and reflectivity to polymeric materials, and for service to the scientific community.

Higgins chaired the [[Advisory Committee on Mathematics Education]] (ACME) from 2008 to 2012.
She is also a former chair (1998–2003) of the Athena Project, which aims for the advancement of women in science, engineering and technology (SET), in Higher Education. Between 2003 and 2007, she was also chair of the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]]. Higgins was president of the [[Institution of Chemical Engineers]] 2002–03, and president of the [[British Association for the Advancement of Science]] 2003–04. She was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1995,<ref name="British Library"/> and was its foreign secretary 2001–06.<ref name="British Library"/>

She is a Fellow of the Institution of Chemical Engineers, [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]],<ref name="List of Fellows">{{cite web| title=List of Fellows| publisher=Royal Academy of Engineering| url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows| access-date=2 July 2022| archive-date=2 April 2019| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402080731/https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows| url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[City and Guilds of London Institute]], of which she is Vice-President. She is an honorary fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and of [[Somerville College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Dame Julia Higgins|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/j.higgins/honours-and-memberships.html|access-date=21 April 2018}}</ref>

She was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 1996, before being named a dame in the 2001 [[Queen's Birthday Honours]] list.<ref name="hons">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/in_depth/uk/2001/birthday_honours_2001/1390779.stm|title=The Queen's birthday Honours|website=News.bbc.co.uk|date=2001|access-date=17 April 2014}}</ref> Dame Julia replaced Professor [[Adrian Smith (statistician)|Adrian Smith]] FRS as ACME Chair in September 2008 when Adrian became Director General of Science and Research at the Department for Innovation, Universities and Skills. She holds honorary degrees from a number of UK universities and the [[University of Melbourne]], Australia. Her scientific work has concentrated on the investigation of polymers with [[neutron scattering]].<ref name="scopus"/> She co-authored a monograph on that field (Higgins & Benoit 1997).<ref>{{cite web
|title=Somerville College Oxford web-site
|url=http://www.some.ox.ac.uk/people/julia-stretton-higgins/
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160724101728/http://www.some.ox.ac.uk/people/julia-stretton-higgins/
|url-status=dead
|archive-date=24 July 2016
|access-date=1 December 2016
|website=Some.ox.ac.uk
}}</ref>

In April 2003, she became chair of the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] and was succeeded by [[John Armitt]] on 1 April 2007. In June 2006, Higgins was appointed principal of the Faculty of engineering at Imperial College London. The Faculty of engineering at Imperial College is one of the largest in the UK, comprising nine departments with 1,000 staff, over 4,200 students and an annual turnover of around £80 million. She is a member of the World Knowledge Dialogue Scientific Board, president of the [[ESPCI|ESPCI ParisTech]] Scientific Committee.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espci.fr/fr/espci-paristech/organisation/conseil-scientifique-international |title=ESPCI Paris : Conseil scientifique international |website=Espci.fr |access-date=10 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720215318/http://www.espci.fr/fr/espci-paristech/organisation/conseil-scientifique-international |archive-date=20 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

She is a Patron of [[The WISE Campaign|WISE]], a charitable organisation that encourages young women to pursue careers in Science, engineering and Construction,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/about_us.cfm |title=About Us |access-date=22 December 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081231204024/http://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/about_us.cfm |archive-date=31 December 2008}}</ref> as well as a member of the Advisory Council for the [[Campaign for Science and Engineering]].<ref name="CaSE Advisory Council">{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |title=Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering |website=Sciencecampaign.org.uk |access-date=11 February 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828110110/http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |archive-date=28 August 2010}}</ref>
On the theme of women in science and engineering, Dame Julia, in May 2014, delivered a lecture entitled "How on Earth did I get here?" to [[Manchester Literary & Philosophical Society ]]  notes of it may be viewed<ref> Manchester Memoirs VOLUME VOLUME 152 2013 - 2014 Memoirs and Proceedings OF THE Manchester Literary & Philosophical Society </ref>

She served as president of the [[Institute of Physics]] from 1 October 2017 to 30 September 2019.<ref name="Institute of Physics News">{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/news/15/may/page_65632.html|title=Dame Julia Higgins to be the IOP's next president-elect|website=Iop.org|access-date=10 July 2015}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Higgins was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1989. Her nomination reads: {{centered pull quote|After obtaining a first degree in Physics the candidate undertook research in the field of [[Physical Chemistry]]. She started using [[neutron scattering]] as a tool for investigating molecular structure and dynamics at this stage, first applying the techniques to the study of [[polymer]]s while a [[postdoctoral research|post-doctoral research assistant]] in the [[School of Chemistry, University of Manchester|Chemistry Department at Manchester]]. She was closely involved with the development of new techniques, their application in [[Polymer science|Polymer Science]] and the formation of an international community of scientists using these techniques while employed as a Physicist at the [[Institut Laue–Langevin|Institut Laue-Langevin]], [[Grenoble]].<ref name="British Library"/>

Since [sic] returning to the UK at Imperial she has built an internationally recognised group. She is well-known for her studies of the dynamics of polymer molecules, especially in the bulk state and, more recently the [[thermodynamics]] and demixing processes in polymer blends. Dr Higgins has a wonderful ability for recognizing when a new area of polymer science is ripe for experimental study and has a row of 'firsts' to her credit.<ref name="royal">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC/1995/11%27) |title=EC/1995/11: Higgins, Dame Julia Stretton |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=31 July 2014 |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/6RTYB2Iih?url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC/1995/11%27) |location=London, UK |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}

Other awards and honours include:
{{div col|colwidth=35em}}
* Principal of the Faculty of engineering (2006–07)
* Chair of the engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (2003 – April 2007)
* Trustee, [[National Gallery]] until 2010<ref name="NG">{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/about-us/organisation/board-of-trustees/minutes-of-the-board/march-2010|title=Board of Trustees|publisher=National Gallery|date=2010|access-date=17 April 2014}}</ref>
* Trustee, [[Daphne Jackson Trust]]
* [[Fellow]] of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]]<ref name="List of Fellows"/>
* Foreign member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] of the United States
* [[Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur]] in 2003
* President, [[British Association for the Advancement of Science]] from 2003 until 2004.
* Received an honorary doctorate from [[Heriot-Watt University]] in 2000<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.hw.ac.uk/graduation/honorary-graduates.htm|title=Heriot-Watt University Edinburgh: Honorary Graduates|website=1.hw.ac.uk|access-date=4 April 2016|archive-date=18 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160418163907/http://www1.hw.ac.uk/graduation/honorary-graduates.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*She is a foreign member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] of the United States. She was named [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) in the [[2001 Birthday Honours]]. In March 2010, the [[UKRC]] announced Professor Higgins as one of six [[Women of Outstanding Achievement Photographic Exhibition|Women of Outstanding Achievement]] in Science, engineering and Technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pandct.com/media/shownews.asp?ID%3D24492 |title=THE uk's MOST OUTSTANDING WOMEN IN SET ANNOUNCED : News from UK Resource Centre for Women (UKRC) |access-date=19 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721032413/http://www.pandct.com/media/shownews.asp?ID=24492 |archive-date=21 July 2011}}</ref>
*A portrait of her by Tess Barnes was unveiled in June 2014 at Imperial College.<ref name=Imp2014>{{cite web|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_23-6-2014-9-56-15|title=Imperial unveils historic portrait of leading female scientist|website=3.imperial.ac.uk|date=23 June 2014 |access-date=10 March 2017}}</ref>
* In 1999 she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng).<ref name="List of Fellows"/> 
* She was chair of the Royal Society's 2008 State of the Nation Report Steering Group for 'Science and mathematics education 14–19'.<ref name=RSSoN>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/projects/state-of-nation/14-19/|title=State of the Nation: Science and mathematics education 14–19|website=royalsociety.org|year=2008|access-date=1 January 2020}}</ref>
* In 2016, she was interviewed by [[Jim Al-Khalili]] on ''[[The Life Scientific]]''.<ref name=tls/>
* Awarded the [[Sir Frank Whittle Medal]] by the Royal Academy of engineering in 2020 "for her sustained excellence in polymer engineering".<ref>{{cite web |title=Sir Frank Whittle Medal |url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/grants-prizes/prizes/prizes-and-medals/individual-medals/whittle-medal |access-date=14 September 2020}}</ref>
{{div col end}}
